exercise.name: Exercise Ball Serratus Wall Slide
aliases: Forearm wall slide on a ball

reference.title: Exercise Ball Serratus Wall Slide
reference.listing: Catalog entry only (gymvisual.com not read; blocked by the proxy). Movement from the exercise name and standard coaching.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the ball rolls up, inhale as it rolls down.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, 0.5 s hold, 2 s down

prescription.progression: Lift the forearms off the ball at the top, or add a mini band around the wrists

cues.text: Face the wall, pin the ball against it with both forearms, elbows bent, palms facing each other.
Breathe out, press into the ball and roll it up the wall, letting the shoulder blades wrap forward.
Reach a little higher without shrugging; ribs down.
Breathe in and roll the ball back down slowly, keeping the pressure on.

mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears; reach forward and up.
Keep pushing into the ball the whole way.
Stand tall; the arms do the work.

kinematics.norm: From about 50 to 130 degrees (clinical opinion); arm elevation with protraction targets the serratus anterior (Ekstrom 2003)
Shoulder blades glide forward as the arms rise (Ludewig 2004)
About 90 degrees, forearms on the ball (standard technique)
Rolls up the wall, centre a constant distance from it (standard technique)

sources.title: GymVisual #20212, Exercise Ball Serratus Wall Slide, video (movement reference)
Ekstrom, Donatelli & Soderberg 2003, surface electromyographic analysis of exercises for the trapezius and serratus anterior muscles (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 33(5):247-258)
Ludewig, Hoff, Osowski, Meschke and Rundquist 2004, relative balance of serratus anterior and upper trapezius muscle activity during push-up exercises (Am J Sports Med 32(2):484-493)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Use a ball rated for exercise, inflated firm.
Shoulder pinching at the top: stop lower.

muscleNotes.serratus_r: Protracts and upwardly rotates the shoulder blade as the arms rise against the ball; wall slides and elevation with protraction are serratus anterior favourites (Ekstrom 2003; Ludewig 2004).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Protracts and upwardly rotates the shoulder blade as the arms rise (Ekstrom 2003; Ludewig 2004).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Assists upward rotation; keep it from shrugging (Ludewig 2004).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Assists upward rotation; keep it from shrugging (Ludewig 2004).
muscleNotes.core: Stops the ribs flaring as the arms go up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Control the shoulder blade on the way down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Control the shoulder blade on the way down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Lengthen as the arms rise (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Lengthen as the arms rise (clinical opinion).
